summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for a non-healing abdominal wound following a prior open gastrostomy tube placement. She underwent reopening and debridement of the wound with removal of a retained suture acting as a foreign body. Postoperatively, she remained stable, afebrile, and in good condition with well-controlled pain. Oral antibiotics were started to prevent infection, and her home medications, including those for glycemic control, were resumed. She tolerated the procedure well and was discharged the following morning with instructions for wound care, antibiotic use, and follow-up with surgery clinic. No complications arose during the brief admission.
problems: Other specified complications of procedures not elsewhere classified
Surgical operation with formation of external stoma causing abnormal patient reaction, or later complication, without mention of misadventure at time of operation
